title: POC Stakeholder Roleplay Runbook + Slide Skeleton
summary: A compact runbook and slide skeleton to run a 3-hour customer POC workshop focused on validating integration points, SLA expectations, and operational handoffs. Emphasis on stakeholder roleplay to flush out acceptance criteria, security concerns, and rollout constraints.
objectives: Validate end-to-end call flow from product UI -> Redwood Hosted API -> backend
Surface non-functional requirements (latency, throughput, isolation) from customer stakeholders
Agree on success criteria and initial rollout plan (canary size, fallback)
agenda: 0:50 - Live roleplay: Product Manager (customer) vs Platform Engineer (redwood) scenario A (30m)
1:30 - Breakout labs: teams prototype API calls and prompts (40m)
2:10 - Consolidation: present breakout outputs and failing cases (25m)
slide_outline: Target architecture diagram (UI, proxy, Redwood routing, KMS)
Breakout lab instructions and success checklist
Proposed rollout plan and measurement plan
facilitation_notes: Keep facilitation tight — roleplay scripts are lightweight prompts, not monologues. Before the roleplay, assign roles explicitly and give 3 minutes to skim scripts. If the roleplay stalls, prompt with escalation triggers: 'customer sees 600ms tail latency spike' or 'unexpected hallucination example' and force decisions (fallback to smaller model, enable reranking). Use the whiteboard to capture decisions with headings: Assumption, Decision, Owner. When technical questions arise that require follow-up (infra quotas, IAM policies, KMS), capture as Jira action immediately with a tentative SLA for response. Encourage customers to call out regulatory constraints early — treat PII/data residency as show-stoppers until validated. For breakouts, pair one customer engineer with one redwood SE — rotate at 20m if multiple teams. End each breakout with a one-slide summary sent to facilitator via Google Slides comment. Note: test demo endpoints before the session and have a static fallback demo (recorded) in case live infra flaps.
prework: Customer: share sample payloads and expected output formats 48h prior
Redwood: provision demo key with restricted scope and send usage instructions 24h prior
All: fill quick context form (link in linked_artifacts) with contact list and escalation phone
success_criteria: Customer can send a sample request and receive expected structured response within SLA window (p95 latency < 350ms)
Agreement on rollout guardrails (canary % and fallback triggers)
List of top 3 unresolved risks with owners and target remediation dates
materials_and_assets: Breakout lab notebook with example curl requests and prompts
logistics: Meeting room with projector + whiteboard. Virtual attendees: Zoom link provided in meeting invite. Reserve breakout rooms in Zoom for two concurrent labs. Catering: light snacks at 1:15pm. Bring a laptop with VPN access if on private deployment demos. Facilitator owns recording consent; record only parts agreed to by customer and mark sensitive slides as 'do not share' in deck comments.
risks_and_mitigations: Live infra instability -> mitigation: switch to recorded demo and run the scripted failures for discussion
Data residency concerns -> mitigation: show private deployment options and KMS flow; mark as escalation for security team
Misaligned success criteria -> mitigation: run quick vote at 2:45 and convert top items into measurable Jira tickets
follow_up_actions: Create Jira epic for POC with tech tasks and owners (due +3 days)
Security review kickoff if PII is involved (owner: Samir Gupta)
Provision dedicated demo capacity if throughput tests required (owner: Diego Alvarez)
Send slide deck and one-slide breakout summaries to attendees within 24h
notes_to_self: Try the new 'small-batch demo' script that exercises prefix caching — it surfaced two sticky edge cases in internal dry run. Keep the roleplay prompts assertive so customers reveal constraints (e.g., "we must operate within 100ms for search box suggestions"). If time gets tight, drop architecture deep-dive and prioritize roleplay + breakout outcomes. Remember to ask legal for NDA template if customer requests recordings.
